We use **Zod 4** (zod ^4). The schema package uses `looseObject` for forward compatibility and Zod's built-in `toJSONSchema` to produce the published JSON Schema, which removes the need for a separate dependency [dec-094vmt9t].

To regenerate the published files (`dist/record.schema.json` and `project.schema.json`), run `pnpm --filter @aimem/schema build`, review the snapshot diff, and update the snapshot deliberately [run-17vbsk09]. A snapshot test (`json-schema.test.ts`) guards the exported contract and was passing on 2026-10-11 [tst-cw10hn77].

Claims are stored as JSON on a separate `aimem-live` branch and acquired with a compare-and-swap: fetch, check the current holder, commit, and push. If the push is rejected, you retry, so two clones can't both win [dec-kqfc1se7].

Related points:
- Claim holders are never written into task files. Live state is kept apart from durable records to avoid merge conflicts on every heartbeat [dec-g17nvbca].
- Trade-offs: it needs network access to the remote, and expired claims can be stolen after the TTL [dec-kqfc1se7].
- A memory record says the same about where claim holders, heartbeat and TTL live (the `aimem-live` branch or a server). It is trust="agent", so it is not human-verified [mem-peqcrkme].

We evaluated isomorphic-git, a pure-JS library, and rejected it because of feature gaps in credentials, hooks and worktrees [dec-ghsxv3vg]. The hoped-for benefits were avoiding process spawning and simpler tests [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Instead, all git work shells out to the user's installed git binary via execa, so credentials, hooks and config behave as usual. Reimplementing git would also miss LFS, worktrees and credential helpers [dec-ndgz6y7a].

The trade-offs: git must be installed (true for every target user) [dec-ndgz6y7a], and tests use real temporary repos instead of mocks [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Counters collide when two branches add records at the same time, so ids are generated randomly (a type prefix plus 8 random Crockford base32 characters) so parallel branches never collide [dec-j2t35mx0].

Trade-offs: ids are not sortable by time, and validation fails on duplicates [dec-j2t35mx0].

After upgrading Biome to 2.5, `biome migrate` rewrote `recommended: true` to `preset: none`, which silently disabled all lint rules [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4]. Lint kept passing because nothing was being checked, so any lint problem could have reached main unnoticed [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4].

It was noticed in the migrate output and fixed the same session (2026-10-12) by setting the preset back to recommended and probing with an explicit `any` [inc-242wrkm4]. Prevention: probe lint after any lint config change, since an explicit `any` should trigger a noExplicitAny warning [inc-242wrkm4][mem-rj2t0xj9].

An unquoted `content_sha` made up only of digits is parsed by YAML as an integer, not a string. The schema's string check on `source.content_sha` then fails with V002. For example, a placeholder sha of zeros became the number 0 and failed validation [mem-hrm4q190].

The fix is to quote hashes and ids that could be all digits when writing frontmatter [mem-hrm4q190].

Note: this record has trust="agent", so it is not human-verified.

aimem authenticates to Google using a service account that can read one shared inbox folder, rather than per-user OAuth [mem-j4yeeebg]. The stated rationale is least privilege and no consent screens for non-developers. Per-user OAuth remains an option [mem-j4yeeebg].

This sits within the broader decision to ingest from Google Drive and upload connectors in v1, producing read-only, externally-owned records [dec-8hscg239].

The records don't describe a way to keep private notes out of git. Related points: records are markdown committed to git as the source of truth [dec-3by2wh28], and roles only affect ranking, not access, so anyone with repo access can read everything [dec-2znaykpx]. The only non-git storage mentioned is the rebuildable vector cache under .aimem/.cache, which is not a place for notes [sch-nygqk0ka].

Token counts are estimated with a heuristic: the number of characters divided by four, with a per-model override available [dec-nppkpt6e]. A real tokenizer differs per model and adds a heavy dependency, so it wasn't used; an optional tokenizer can be installed later [dec-nppkpt6e].

The estimate can be off by roughly 10–20%, so per-section limits are given some headroom [dec-nppkpt6e].

For context, the default briefing budget is 4000 tokens unless project.yaml sets briefing.budget_tokens [mem-q9krtm0g].

No. The Odoo connector is deferred. The decision postpones Odoo sync, keeps the design, and states that nothing in v1 depends on it [dec-bgh1zcas]. Milestone M4b ships upload and Google only [dec-bgh1zcas]. The `odoo` value stays reserved in `source.system` [dec-bgh1zcas].

The project uses **Biome** for linting and formatting, not ESLint/Prettier.

- A verified record describes upgrading Biome to 2.5 and its `migrate` command, which touched the linter config; it also mentions `noExplicitAny` as a lint rule that should fire [mem-rj2t0xj9].
- An inferred (not human-verified) record claims ESLint and Prettier, but it says this came from the alternatives column of the tech stack doc, contradicts `biome.json`, and needs review [mem-yd7935cw]. I'd treat it as wrong.

One caveat: after the Biome 2.5 migration, the config had been rewritten to `preset: none`, which disables all lint rules. It should be set to `recommended` [mem-rj2t0xj9].

Per the planned design, yes. The accepted, verified decision is hybrid retrieval: briefings fuse BM25 with a local multilingual embedding model, and fall back to lexical-only when no model is present [dec-mtbcq7yr]. A related task (open) covers building the embeddings behind an interface, with a lexical fallback [tsk-w4411vwr].

Caveats:
- A memory claims search is lexical-only BM25 without embeddings. It is inferred (not human-verified), is based on an ADR marked superseded, and is flagged as needing review, so I wouldn't rely on it [mem-1x4y6jd8].
- The embeddings and the BM25 index/search tasks are both still open [tsk-w4411vwr][tsk-7hfeytzh], so the records don't confirm embeddings are implemented yet.
- The draft core search is described as keyword-based (the draft uses MiniSearch) [tsk-7hfeytzh]. That handoff is agent-written, not human-verified [hnd-hqq0tyzk].
- The choice of embedding model is still only proposed [dec-f30g1hx1].

It depends on the mode. In solo mode, agents commit (solo implies `agent_commits: commit`). In team mode, the default is `stage`, so agents stage changes and humans commit them along with their code. A `pr` option is also available [dec-ek66gxgx].

A new decision with no explicit status gets **proposed**. This matches the spec 03 lifecycle (proposed, then accepted or rejected) [dec-9h7m0yg3]. Agents must pass `--status accepted` when a human has already agreed [dec-9h7m0yg3].

History: an earlier schema draft had `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = accepted`, which the spec did not contain. That was flagged in a handoff (agent-written, not human-verified) [hnd-qp6gjbe5]. The verified decision above supersedes it.

Run the "full local check" runbook, which is verified [run-gea7sjyn]:

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm lint`
3. `pnpm typecheck`
4. `pnpm test`

It passes when all three checks (lint, typecheck, test) exit 0. There is nothing to roll back [run-gea7sjyn]. The same gate, `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`, is what CI runs on Linux and macOS with Node 22 and 24 [mem-rmqc83gx]. Tests include property tests, so a failure may show a shrunk counterexample [mem-rmqc83gx].

The release checklist record (agent-written, not human-verified) lists "run the full local check" as its first step before changelog, tag and publish [mem-pq7r2x9k].
